name: mirror_dirty_parity
face_ring_start_note: A mirror emits one new face per source face, and measured 2026-08-18 the MIRRORED half disagrees on ring start in every case while the original half agrees in every case -- 63 of 126 rings, exactly the images. Both sides hold the same corners and both reverse the winding, so what is unported is only where the reflected ring is cut. Filed in doc/tasks/backlog/1311-ring-start-laws-to-capture.md; the half-and-half split is itself the evidence that the recorded starts are a stable property of the reference and not capture noise.
description: Mirroring a whole layer through a world plane, with and without the seam weld, over non-planar / reflex / poled / degenerate / counter-wound bases. No fixture measured this command before.

provenance.notes: The weld distance is the interesting axis: the y-plane cells sit ON the mirror plane with the weld off, so every vertex doubles, while the x-plane cells weld a seam whose vertices are 1e-3 apart. Frozen face rings carry the winding, which a mirror is expected to reverse. CHANNELS: the sweep's comparison was never vertex-only -- it compared the vertex multiset, the edge multiset, faces BOTH as ordered rings (winding shows) and as unordered position sets, the material partition, the per-face 'did this face's own tag change', and the post-command selection. Re-checked independently over all 215 frozen cases: ZERO agree on vertices while differing on ordered face rings, so nothing frozen here is a vertex-channel-only agreement. PRECISION: the sweep compared at 1e-4 and this fixture's tolerance matches it. The actual reproduction is far tighter -- 208 of the 215 cases are bit-identical at the dumps' 6 decimals and the remaining 7 agree to 3e-6 or better, that being the worst deviation anywhere in the set. The tolerance is the MEASUREMENT's bound, not the data's.
